codeReview.summary: Solid, complete implementation of Pov and PovCriteria models and DAOs with comprehensive test coverage. All 6 files are well-structured, follow the existing TimeEntryDao pattern precisely, use PreparedStatement throughout, and handle null fields safely. Cascade delete is correctly implemented via ON DELETE CASCADE in the DatabaseInitializer schema. The 47 tests (23 PovDaoTest + 24 PovCriteriaDaoTest) cover all CRUD operations, edge cases (null fields, non-existent IDs, SQL injection), cascade delete behavior, timestamp management, and all status/weight values. No blocking issues found.

issues.description: Thread.sleep(10) is used to ensure timestamp ordering in findAll_orderedByCreatedAtDesc. While this works and is a common pattern, it could theoretically be flaky on an extremely slow system. The sleep values (10ms, 50ms) are reasonable and this pattern matches the codebase convention.

create() and update() mutate the input Pov object directly (setting timestamps and ID). This is consistent with the existing TimeEntryDao pattern but means callers must be aware the input object is modified. Not a bug — just a pattern note.

PovCriteriaDao.update() does not update pov_id, meaning a criterion cannot be reassigned to a different POV via update. This is actually correct behavior (FK should remain stable), and the test update_preservesPovId explicitly verifies this. Documenting as intentional design.

summary: Feature pov-model-dao passes review. The implementation is complete, correct, and well-tested. Both Pov and PovCriteria models have all specified fields with getters/setters. PovDao provides findAll(), findById(), create(), update(), delete() — all using PreparedStatement. PovCriteriaDao provides findByPovId(), findById(), create(), update(), delete() — all using PreparedStatement. Cascade delete from POV to criteria is implemented via ON DELETE CASCADE in the database schema and verified by tests. 47 JUnit 5 tests pass covering all CRUD methods, edge cases, null handling, cascade behavior, timestamp management, and SQL injection safety. The code follows existing codebase patterns (TimeEntryDao) consistently. No blocking issues found.
